I can give you a concise but thorough overview of the Malta Memorial and what it commemorates, and I can look up or confirm exact details (dates, numbers, inscriptions, designer) if you want.

What the Malta Memorial is
- The Malta Memorial is a Commonwealth War Graves Commission (CWGC) monument in Malta that commemorates members of the Commonwealth air forces who lost their lives while serving in the Mediterranean and the surrounding area and who have no known grave.
- It is dedicated specifically to aircrew who were lost in operations based on, or operating from, Malta and the wider Mediterranean theatre during the Second World War (and related campaigns) and whose bodies were never recovered or identified.

Location and setting
- The memorial is situated on Malta (close to Valletta/Floriana) in a public gardened area and is intentionally prominent so it can be visited by relatives, servicemen, and the public. The CWGC maintains the memorial and its surroundings.

Design and appearance (summary)
- The structure is a formal monument that includes sculptural elements and panels on which the names of the missing are inscribed. Its style and materials reflect the CWGC’s post‑war memorial language of dignified, durable stone and bronze inscriptions.
- The memorial is designed to be a place for reflection and remembrance for those who have no known grave.

Purpose and significance
- The memorial commemorates servicemen from across the Commonwealth air forces — including the Royal Air Force, Royal Australian Air Force, Royal Canadian Air Force, Royal New Zealand Air Force, and other Commonwealth air personnel — who were lost over the Mediterranean and surrounding theatres and have no known resting place.
- It symbolizes both the strategic importance of Malta during WWII (as a forward base for Allied air and naval operations in the Mediterranean) and the high human cost paid by aircrews operating from and around the island.
- It is one of several CWGC memorials around the world that record names of the missing when no recoverable grave exists.

Commemoration and use
- The memorial is used for official remembrance ceremonies and is a focus for relatives of the missing and visiting veterans.
- The CWGC keeps records associated with those commemorated and can provide information to relatives and researchers.

- the date of unveiling and who performed the unveiling,
- the full inscription text and/or notable names on the memorial,
- visiting details (exact location, opening/access, nearest landmarks),
- historical context about operations from Malta that led to the losses commemorated.

Which of those specific details would you like me to fetch and confirm?
